units.title: Unit 23 — Films and books
units.source: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition); printed pages 50–51 (PDF pages 54–55).
units.bookTitle: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition)
units.category: Leisure and lifestyle · films, literature and reviews
learningObjectives: Discuss new film and book releases, reviews, critics and the difference between reviewing and criticising.
Describe narratives naturally using character, opening and closing, atmosphere and ending collocations.
Talk about acting, film-making, casting, roles, special effects and box-office success.
Use collocations for reading habits, audiobooks and e-books and distinguish watch television from see a film at the cinema.

items.pt: um livro é lançado; um livro sai
items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: Her first book comes out at the end of November.
items.note: Come out is an intransitive phrasal verb used for the release of a new book, film or recording.

items.pt: um filme estreia; um filme é lançado
items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The new science-fiction film comes out next Friday.
items.note: A film comes out when it becomes available to the public, especially in cinemas.

items.pt: resenhar um livro; fazer uma crítica de um livro
items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: Our literature tutor asked us to review a book for the class blog.
items.note: Review means assess a work and describe its qualities; it does not necessarily mean criticise it negatively.

items.pt: fazer uma crítica de um filme; resenhar um filme
items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: A local journalist will review the film after tonight's screening.
items.note: A review can be positive, negative or mixed; criticise usually suggests finding fault.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: A book reviewer praised the author's clear writing style.
items.note: A person who evaluates books for a publication or website, not just someone who reads them.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: A film critic discussed the director's unusual choice of music.
items.note: A critic writes or speaks professionally about films; their judgement need not be negative.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: I read a book review before buying the novel.
items.note: A written or spoken evaluation of a book; not merely a summary of its plot.

items.pt: crítica de filme; resenha de filme
items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The film review highlighted the strength of the acting.
items.note: A review assesses a film and often explains the reviewer's opinion.

items.pt: fazer uma avaliação negativa; dar uma crítica desfavorável
items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: Several critics gave the comedy a bad review after its premiere.
items.note: Give a review expresses an evaluation; a bad review specifically reports an unfavourable judgement.

items.word: be based on a true story
items.pt: ser baseado em uma história real
items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The drama is based on a true story about a rescue at sea.
items.note: Based on signals that the narrative draws on actual events; details may still be fictionalised.

items.pt: captar a atmosfera; transmitir o clima
items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The opening scene captures the atmosphere of a busy night market.
items.note: Capture the atmosphere means communicate the distinctive mood or feeling of a place or period.

items.pt: abordar um tema; tratar de um assunto
items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The documentary deals with a topic that affects many small towns.
items.note: Deal with introduces a subject that a book, film or discussion examines.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The opening scenes introduce the two main families.
items.note: Opening refers to the first scenes in a film; compare the opening chapters of a book.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The closing scenes show what happens to the characters years later.
items.note: Closing refers to the last scenes of a film, not necessarily to the credits.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The opening chapters establish why the brothers stopped speaking.
items.note: Chapters are divisions of a book; opening specifies those at the beginning.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The closing chapter reveals the secret behind the missing letter.
items.note: The closing chapter is the final chapter; opening chapter refers to the first.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The beginning of the book is slow, but the story soon becomes exciting.
items.note: Beginning is usual for the first part of a story; start of a book is less typical in this context.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: We were surprised by the end of the film.
items.note: End is the usual noun for the final part of a book or film, rather than finish.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: The central characters have very different attitudes to risk.
items.note: Central characters are essential to the story; they need not be heroic or likeable.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: I wanted the story to have a happy ending after all that tension.
items.note: Happy ending is the usual expression for a positive conclusion to a story.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: I often recommend a book to colleagues who enjoy history.
items.note: Use recommend something to someone, not recommend someone a book in standard usage.

items.section: A · Talking about films and books
items.example: This short novel is highly recommended for intermediate readers.
items.note: Highly is the conventional intensifier with recommended; very recommended is unnatural.

items.pt: seguir a carreira de ator; atuar profissionalmente
items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: She hopes to go on the stage after finishing drama school.
items.note: This expression means become a professional actor, especially in theatre; it is not merely stepping onto a platform.

items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: An independent company agreed to produce a film about the expedition.
items.note: Produce focuses on organising and financing film-making; direct refers to creative direction.

items.pt: um drama histórico; um filme de época
items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: They watched a historical drama set in eighteenth-century Scotland.
items.note: A drama whose action is set in a past historical period.

items.pt: o cinema; a tela do cinema
items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The landscape looked spectacular on the big screen.
items.note: The big screen refers to cinema, particularly in contrast with television or mobile devices.

items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The students hope to make a film about life in their neighbourhood.
items.note: Make a film is a broad term for film production; shoot a film emphasises recording the scenes.

items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The director decided to use special effects for the storm sequence.
items.note: Special effects create visual or other effects that would be difficult to film directly.

items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The battle scenes required careful planning and a large cast.
items.note: Scenes showing combat in a film; battle is the conventional noun modifier here.

items.pt: o protagonista masculino; o papel principal masculino
items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The male lead gives a quiet but convincing performance.
items.note: Lead refers to a principal role or the actor playing it; its pronunciation here is /liːd/.

items.pt: a protagonista feminina; o papel principal feminino
items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The female lead received excellent reviews for her acting.
items.note: Lead denotes the leading role, not the actor's position in the credits alone.

items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: In the new drama, he will play the role of a young scientist.
items.note: Play the role of is a natural verb phrase for acting as a particular character.

items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The veteran actor agreed to take on a cameo role in the comedy.
items.note: A cameo role is a brief, distinctive appearance by an actor; take on means accept the part.

items.pt: fazer uma excelente atuação; ter um excelente desempenho
items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The young actor gave an excellent performance in her first major role.
items.note: Give a performance describes acting, music and similar artistic work.

items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The animated feature may be nominated for an Oscar this year.
items.note: Be nominated for means be formally proposed for an award; nomination does not mean winning it.

items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The comedy became an immediate box-office hit despite mixed reviews.
items.note: Box-office hit emphasises commercial success with cinema audiences.

items.pt: apresentar-se para salas lotadas; atrair público de casa cheia
items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The musical played to full houses throughout its first month.
items.note: A full house is a cinema or theatre audience with no vacant seats; plural full houses covers repeated shows.

items.pt: escolher o elenco de um filme
items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: The producers hired a specialist to cast the film.
items.note: Cast a film means select the actors, not film the scenes.

items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: She will star in a film about a musician's early career.
items.note: Star in means perform in a prominent role, rather than merely appear briefly.

items.pt: filmar um filme; rodar um filme
items.section: B · Just about films and acting
items.example: They plan to shoot a film in the mountains next spring.
items.note: Shoot is a production verb meaning record the images for a film.

items.pt: estar completamente absorvido na leitura de um livro
items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: He was engrossed in a book and almost missed his stop.
items.note: Engrossed in means so interested that attention to other things decreases.

items.pt: estar imerso na leitura de um livro
items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: She was absorbed in a book when the lights went out.
items.note: Absorbed in is close in meaning to engrossed in and describes deep concentration.

items.pt: leitura viciante; leitura que prende muito a atenção
items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: The journalist's account of the rescue makes compulsive reading.
items.note: Compulsive reading is writing so engaging that the reader wants to continue.

items.pt: leitura antes de dormir; leitura de cabeceira
items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: She keeps a collection of short stories for bedtime reading.
items.note: Bedtime reading describes what someone reads before going to sleep.

items.pt: uma leitura fácil; um livro de leitura leve
items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: The mystery is an easy read, even if you are travelling.
items.note: An easy read is a book that is not difficult or demanding to read.

items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: You can download an audiobook to listen to during the flight.
items.note: An audiobook contains a spoken recording of a book.

items.pt: baixar um aplicativo de leitura de e-books
items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: I had to download an e-book reader app before opening the file.
items.note: The app displays electronic books; it is different from downloading a book itself.

items.pt: os lançamentos mais recentes de livros
items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: The shop posts a list of the latest book releases every Monday.
items.note: Book release is the publication of a new title; latest describes the newest ones.

items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: He flicked through a book while waiting for the appointment.
items.note: Flick through suggests turning pages quickly without close reading.

items.pt: passar os olhos por um livro; ler por alto
items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: Before the interview, she skimmed through a book about the company.
items.note: Skim through suggests reading quickly to get the main ideas, rather than studying every detail.

items.section: C · Just about books, audiobooks and e-books
items.example: Her first novel is beautifully written and full of memorable dialogue.
items.note: Beautifully modifies written to praise the quality or style of the writing.

items.section: D · Common mistakes and meaning contrasts
items.example: We hardly ever watch television during the week.
items.note: Watch television is idiomatic for the activity; see television is not normally used in this sense.

items.word: see a film at the cinema
items.pt: assistir a um filme no cinema
items.section: D · Common mistakes and meaning contrasts
items.example: We're going to see a film at the cinema after work.
items.note: See a film is the usual choice for a cinema visit; see or watch can be used for a film on television.

units.title: Unit 24 — Music
units.source: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition); printed pages 52–53 (PDF pages 56–57).
units.bookTitle: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition)
units.category: Leisure and lifestyle · music, musicians and performances
learningObjectives: Describe recordings and musical styles using expressions for albums, hits, tunes and different kinds of performances.
Discuss musicians, audiences, touring, musical heritage and making, composing and releasing music.
Talk about musical instruments and learning to play, including take up, tune, strum and play a piece.
Recognise natural contrasts in music-related language such as big versus minor hit, live versus recorded performance and lover versus liker.

items.pt: a cena do rock; o cenário musical do rock
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: Several new groups have joined the local rock music scene.
items.note: Music scene denotes the musicians, venues, listeners and activity in a particular musical community.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The singer's first single made a big impact on local radio.
items.note: Make an impact describes having a noticeable effect; big and major are natural modifiers.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: Soft background music was playing in the café.
items.note: Background music is not normally the main focus of listeners' attention.

items.pt: sair muito alto das caixas de som; tocar aos berros
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: Heavy metal was blasting out from the speakers next door.
items.note: Blast out indicates very loud sound; from introduces where the sound is coming from.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: Her debut album reached the charts within a week.
items.note: Debut marks a musician's or band's first publicly released album.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The live performance attracted a larger audience than expected.
items.note: Live here is pronounced /laɪv/ and contrasts with pre-recorded performance.

items.pt: música leve e fácil de ouvir
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: My grandfather often chooses easy listening for long journeys.
items.note: A label for accessible, undemanding music, not a comment on listening skill.

items.pt: uma melodia cativante; uma música que fica na cabeça
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The advert uses a catchy tune that everyone remembers.
items.note: Catchy describes music that is easy to remember and repeat.

items.pt: fazer uma apresentação sentimental; interpretar de modo emotivo
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The pianist gave a sentimental performance of the old love song.
items.note: Sentimental describes the emotional tone of a performance; it can be positive or mildly critical.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The young singer became a pop idol after her first tour.
items.note: A pop idol is a highly admired pop star with devoted fans.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: Adoring fans waited for the band outside the venue.
items.note: Adoring emphasises strong affection or admiration for a performer.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The group recorded a rock symphony with a full orchestra.
items.note: A work that combines rock features with elements of symphonic composition.

items.pt: uma peça musical; uma composição musical
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: She played a short piece of music at the ceremony.
items.note: Piece of music is a flexible phrase for a musical work or passage.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: Their second single was a massive hit across Europe.
items.note: Massive hit is stronger than minor hit and stresses exceptional popularity.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The song became a big hit on streaming platforms.
items.note: A big hit means a very successful recording, concert or other artistic work.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The band expects to release an album in the spring.
items.note: Release an album is the standard expression for making a recording publicly available.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: Her brother wrote the music for the new play.
items.note: Write the music means compose it, rather than perform or record it.

items.pt: ter muitos seguidores; contar com uma enorme base de fãs
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The singer has a huge following in South America.
items.note: Following is a collective noun for supporters or fans, not just social-media followers.

items.pt: sair em turnê; fazer uma turnê
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The jazz quartet will go on tour after releasing its album.
items.note: Go on tour means travel to perform a series of concerts or shows.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The film's haunting melodies stayed with me for days.
items.note: Haunting describes music that is emotionally powerful and hard to forget.

items.pt: uma apresentação de virtuosismo; uma performance magistral
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The violinist gave a virtuoso performance at the festival.
items.note: Virtuoso emphasises exceptional technical skill, not simply an enjoyable performance.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The festival hopes to capture a wider audience for classical music.
items.note: Capture an audience suggests attracting and engaging listeners or viewers.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The museum celebrates the region's musical heritage.
items.note: Heritage refers to musical traditions passed down through a culture or community.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: A guest musician will conduct the orchestra during the concert.
items.note: Conduct is the established verb for directing an orchestra as it performs.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: She plans to compose a piece for piano and cello.
items.note: Compose describes creating music; conduct describes directing its performance.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: As a classical music lover, he often attends chamber concerts.
items.note: Music lover expresses a strong enjoyment of a genre; not music liker.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The group released a double album with twenty new tracks.
items.note: A double album is a recording issued as a two-part or two-disc album.

items.pt: contar com a participação de um artista; destacar um artista
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The new track features an artist from Lisbon.
items.note: Feature means include someone as a notable contributor; the artist need not be the main performer.

items.pt: um artista de rap; um rapper
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: A rap artist opened the show with a new song.
items.note: Rap artist refers to someone who performs rap, typically rhythmic spoken lyrics.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The hip-hop band worked with a local jazz trio.
items.note: Hip-hop identifies the genre or musical tradition associated with the group.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: After ten years with the group, she decided to go solo.
items.note: Go solo means start performing independently rather than as a band member.

items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The producer offered to remix a track for the next release.
items.note: Remix means create a new version of an existing recording, often by changing its sound or arrangement.

items.pt: músicas de ritmo acelerado; faixas animadas
items.section: A · Describing music
items.example: The concert ended with three up-tempo numbers.
items.note: Up-tempo means played with a fast beat; number can refer to a performed song.

items.pt: dedilhar ou tocar as cordas de um violão com movimentos de varredura
items.section: B · Playing music
items.example: He sat on the balcony and strummed a guitar while his friends sang.
items.note: Strum involves brushing fingers or a pick across several strings, unlike plucking individual notes.

items.pt: começar a aprender a tocar violão ou guitarra
items.section: B · Playing music
items.example: I decided to take up the guitar after hearing a live concert.
items.note: Take up means begin learning an activity or instrument, especially as a hobby.

items.section: B · Playing music
items.example: She clearly has musical talent, although she has never had lessons.
items.note: Musical talent refers to natural ability in music, not necessarily professional training.

items.section: B · Playing music
items.example: The restaurant offers live music on Friday evenings.
items.note: Live music is performed in real time; live is pronounced /laɪv/.

items.section: B · Playing music
items.example: The players need to tune their instruments before the rehearsal.
items.note: Tune means adjust an instrument to produce the correct pitches.

items.pt: executar uma peça musical; tocar uma composição
items.section: B · Playing music
items.example: The student will play a piece by a contemporary composer.
items.note: A piece is a musical composition or extract; play here means perform it.

items.pt: apreciadores de música folk; fãs de música folclórica
items.section: D · Exercise-based usage contrasts
items.example: The small festival brings together folk music lovers from several regions.
items.note: Lover, rather than liker, is the idiomatic noun for a devoted enthusiast.

items.pt: fazer uma apresentação maravilhosa; ter um desempenho excelente
items.section: D · Exercise-based usage contrasts
items.example: The choir gave a wonderful performance on Saturday night.
items.note: Give a performance, not do a performance, is the idiomatic artistic combination.

items.section: D · Exercise-based usage contrasts
items.example: Learning a musical instrument requires regular practice.
items.note: Musical instrument is the normal noun phrase for a tool used to make music.
